page.layout: One column of italic verse, stanzas set in full lines; the page number and running head at the top; the catchword "Præfens" at the lower right.

l.i: Et quodcunque locis spirat in omnibus.
At tu, præ reliquis, sancta Dei cohors,
Ter defuncta malis, monstra quot unico
Laudes pange Deo: qui Sisaram malum
Salmunam, Iabin, Og, cum Seono Zebum,
pij Natum concelebrant: debuit is mori
Christum qui vetuit nasci: o Deus,
Qua fulcire velis numine qui tuo
Durant, terra licet deneget his opem.
Regni septa tui perdita qui volunt,

page.notes: Ornamental marks (dingbats or fleurons) stand before "Mutet", "Aër", "Et" and "Alcides" and before the line "Sic HENRICE"; they are not transcribed as text. "HENRICE" is set in small capitals; "Sic" appears roman. The word "secuit" is read from a long s and could be "fecuit"; I have read it as secuit. "Humanoq;" has a q-with-tail abbreviation for -que, kept as printed. The long s has been rendered as a plain s throughout. The word "Præfens" at the lower right is the catchword for the next page.
